sentence: This project tests whether the brain systems that control attention and arousal change activity in memory centers when the focus of attention shifts.
This project builds and tests tools that use electronic health records to find patients with HIV who would benefit from proactive support.
This project studies how different parts of the mouse cortex hold information in working memory, using virtual reality and recordings of neural activity.
This project studies how chronic infection with Trypanosoma cruzi leads to inflammation and cardiac fibrosis.
This project studies the gene networks involved in how the meninges form and how meningiomas grow.
This project builds an automated platform that maps proteins inside cells and tests it in healthy and fibrotic human lung tissue.
This project offers data science advice and shared computing resources to help members of a center use environmental health data.
This project tests whether mutations in hematopoietic stem cells that arise with aging make periodontal disease more severe.
This project develops ways to tell normal from abnormal phosphorylation of a protein found in Lewy bodies in diseased brains.
This project builds a nanopore method to check the quality of adeno-associated virus capsids used in gene therapy.
This project uses single-cell sequencing to study how mutations give small populations of cells in normal tissues a growth advantage.
This project develops a vaccine on a liposome nanoparticle and tests how well it protects against tuberculosis in murine and guinea pig models.
This project develops assays to find natural products that may stop pancreatic cancer from progressing from pre-invasive to invasive.
This project tests in humans whether self-amplifying mRNA vaccines can start the maturation of broadly neutralizing antibodies.
This project tests a laser and ultrasound imaging method that uses particles carrying dyes to tell aggressive from non-aggressive prostate cancer in mouse models.
This project tests chemical treatments to find ones that improve length of life and quality of aging in a simple animal model.
This project uses mutant mice, induced pluripotent stem cells and zebrafish to study the genetic causes of craniofacial disorders.
This project helps inventors define clinical needs, test and refine diagnostic technologies built from microsystems.
This project studies how two signaling pathways guide human lung development and how variants in genes cause lethal lung developmental disorders in neonates.
This project identifies the mutational factors shaping melanocytes in normal human skin.
